utterances.text: It was on the Saturday of 17th April, 1993. And as far as the shelling is concerned, that started earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very well. Very well.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: It's not very well. That's how it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Will you please be so kind and just listen to my questions. Where were you on the 17th of April at 8.00?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: I was at home.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Will you please take your statement, turn to page 2, and look at paragraph 2 from the bottom, because you say there: "When the attack started, I was at the position called Kamen." In other words, you were not at home. You were on the position.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: I was at home when the shelling of Mackovice started, but it was so close that it took me only several minutes to reach my position.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And you saw the village being shelled?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Okay. Now, move down to the next paragraph. It says: "I was in a trench with a fellow soldier when the attack started, and I had my back towards the village so that I could not see the shelling of the village."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Yes. That is my vantage point, but I could not see the exact houses that were being hit, but of course I was aware of the fact that the village was being shelled.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So what is written in this statement is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we go into the private session now? I'm going to need to mention some names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very well. To quote you, let's go to the main thing. So please tell me, how long did you observe the man whom you called Tuta? And how did you know that this was Tuta and not someone else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Because when they took us prisoner, it was four Croat soldiers, and when they were tying our hands, they told us that they had to turn us over to Mr. Tuta, and then --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Excuse me, just a moment. So four men told you that they were taking you to Tuta?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And to whom did they bring you? You said that there were 100 soldiers there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Just a moment. 100 soldiers. You even said today up to 200?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: 100 to 200. There were a lot of soldiers; that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And now, how did you know and what did they say? "Here, this is Tuta"? Is that how it was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: They did not say that this was Tuta, but they brought us into a circle of soldiers and Tuta was in front of them, and we saw that he is the main one, the one in charge.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: When you say that Tuta was in front of them, how did you know that it was Tuta?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Because they told us that they were taking us to Tuta. He was there in front of the soldiers. So he was the main one, because he was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: In other words, Witness, you concluded?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So this is your inference, conclusion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Had anyone else stood in front of the soldiers, you would have made the same conclusion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Later on, when I was shown pictures, I concluded that it was him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And also, do you allow, when you concluded that, that perhaps it was not Tuta?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: I cannot conclude that he was not Tuta when he was. In Sarajevo, they asked me whether that was the man, and I said it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Now, tell me, please, how thick were the glasses that this man that you called Tuta had?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: It was thick.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: We can see your fingers. Perhaps you can show us.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Well, rather thick. Not too much, but they were not regular.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can we say that they were two to three centimetres thick?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: No, we cannot say that. And I was too far, so I wasn't able to say how far, and again, I wasn't free to observe very clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You weren't free to look, but you still made a conclusion, and you still made this observation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: But later on, when I was made to pick grapes, the grapes, that's when I looked at him very clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, how many pictures did they show you in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Quite a few, ten.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: His?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Different ones. And they asked me which one was his, so that they would be assured that I was clear on who he was. And then -- and then this American lawyer said that this was true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And tell me, what are these American forces which interviewed you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Well, that lawyer who investigated that statement, whether that was so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did everybody wear a beard and have hair and glasses on the photographs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: No, they didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, please, are you still -- that to this day, you did not know what that man's hair is coloured and how long it was and what colour it was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: No. All I remember is grey beard, glasses, and that is it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And how tall was he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: How tall? Well, about 185, thereabouts. Rather tall.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Rather tall. And what about his age?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Well, I said 35 then, but I think he was older.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: But you said 35 where?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: In the statement. I think that is what the statement said. But he was much older. It was simply fear.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Fear of whom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Well, well, at that time, about his years, a few years more. I couldn't really say exactly because I was very afraid.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, how was this man built?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Well, just simple.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Like you, or as I -- I mean, as I see you or as you see me, was he bigger, stronger?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Well, no, like me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Like you. Could you please straighten up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Yeah, sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And what about your weight? How much do you weigh?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Now, I'm 102 kilogrammes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that the reason for the beating was to find out what kind of communication you had with Jablanica and the like, isn't it, when you were asked questions by the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: But you see in your statement which you gave over there -- and you have it here, too. That is page -- let me see which one it is. The fourth, page 4.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Yeah, 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: That's right. You said that he beat him in order to find out who was the -- who was your group's commander.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Yes, group's, yes. He knew who was the commander, because otherwise he wouldn't have called Dzemal. But he wanted to find out who was the group leader, whether we had communication with Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness RR, I'm being warned that my last question when I asked if he looked like you, that was not in the transcript. And then you said that he looked like you, and then I asked you how much did you weigh and what did you say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: I said 102 kilograms.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And you said he looked like you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Well, yes. He's roughly my build.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Your build. Aha, I see. Thank you very much. It is only for the record. I apologise, Witness RR. I have to do it once again. So my question was: Was he built like you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Yes, he's about my height, my build.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You said that you had to keep your head down throughout?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Yes, except when I picked grapes. Then I had to get those grapes from the hands.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And tell me, do you know who were those soldiers who happened to be there, those 100, 200 soldiers? Where did they come from? Who were they? What were they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Well, they were from Jablanica, because they had come out from there, and Prozor had fallen, and they were in Doljani accommodated. That is, soldiers -- the Croat council from the Jablanica municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And those were those men by whom you were encircled in front of that hut?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: And there were some soldiers that I didn't know. Tuta's troops who had taken the village, Duga Grude, and --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, please, how do you know that they were Tuta's troops? How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: We know it because that one from Jablanica, Blaz, he was in Croat -- I mean Tuta's army. And Tuta also called that Dzemal, so one knew it was Tuta's troops. And this one from Junozovici, our Muslim who was in his army, and he knew that it was his army.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So tell me, please, what is this Blaz's last name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Blaz -- I can't remember his last name.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Mm-hm. And then it was only through these two that you concluded that everybody else was Tuta's men, or what you said Tuta's army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Tuta's army, yes, Tuta's troops.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And on the base of that, you again conjectured that it was Tuta's army on the base of those two?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: No, not those two unknown soldiers. Tuta's troops, Tuta's army, Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. because they said they were going to turn us over to Tuta's troops, to Tuta's army.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did they have any patches, any insignia on their uniforms? Did they have any markings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Well, on their shoulders, they had HVO patches.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And that Tuta called Dzemal, that's the story that you told us before, is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Yes, yes. About those. That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Aha. Very well. Now, tell me, was there -- excuse me. Was there somebody -- I think you mentioned somebody minor, somebody who was underage.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Oh, Fikret Tasic, who was in the camp, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: No, no, I mean in front of the house in Doljani.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Oh, yes, Denis Skender.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And he was released and taken to the school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: He was taken to the school. He was underage. Neighbours took him to the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Oh, and neighbours did. And nobody touched him, did they? --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Well, at the time when we were captured, our hands were tied, and he was behind our backs. And he was saying that he was simply found there with his pals, that he had done nothing, and he was crying and begging them let him go. So they did let him go, and it was only later that I learned that he had been transferred to the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I see. And tell me, then, they put you, you say, into a red car, Niva make --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Yes, Niva.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: What is it, Lada Niva?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: No -- yes, it is Lada Niva.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: How many people can fit into that Lada Niva?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: How many? I don't know. But they loaded us all into that Niva.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: How many?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Eight of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Eight of you. And they loaded you all into the Lada Niva?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: It's a story we used to tell at school, "How many people can you fit into a Lada?"

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's why I asked. Because we have the same story, about Zaporozec, and about Ladas. Zaporozec is that other car.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Right. So and how many men guarded you? Were you alone with the driver?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Next to the driver was a soldier who ordered us not to -- not to look up, and he had the rifle with him. So there were two of them in front.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very well. Now, tell us, as you were driving towards Ljubuski -- that is, you were moving towards Obruc and then to Sovicka Vrata. If I am correct, you took that road. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And you said that you saw a cow shed on fire, that it was some neighbour's of yours, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Yes, Kukic's cow shed. When we got out of the vehicle, because the car couldn't get out, so he told us to get off. And then we looked around and saw Kukic's cow shed on fire and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Aha, very well. And tell us, did those soldiers treat you well? Did they treat you to beer, to Coca-Cola?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Yes, they gave us some juices.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Mm-hm. I see. Very well. And now, you arrived in Ljubuski. Now you see we are moving there. We are in Ljubuski now. And you said that you couldn't go to toilet and things like that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Yes, we were locked up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Right. But now, will you please have a look -- it is page 7, if I'm correct. Will you please turn it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Sure, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Now, one, two, three, four, five, sixth passage from above?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And you say: "First we were not permitted to go to the toilet. We were given some bottles to relieve in."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: "We could use the toilet only on our way to meals, and we ate standing in the yard."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Yes, that's so. It is true. On Sundays, we could do our laundry and clean the cell.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes, is that so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Now, tell me, but were you treated correctly at Ljubuski? You, you personally, were you treated correctly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Well, rather.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And what about others? I mean, I'm asking you. Give me a candid answer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Well, no, because Dzemal Ovnovic was beaten and others and others too who were brought from Prozor seven days later, Hasib Lulic and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: But otherwise, what was the treatment like? Was it correct? Was it okay?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Why, yes, in comparison with what went on in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I apologise. I have to take you back a little to that hut before you got to Ljubuski to tell us how is it that Tuta struck -- strike that man? You say that Tuta beat him. Now --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Now, with what hand did he beat him, and how did he hold that pistol?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Well, as I picked those grapes and I looked to the left and Fikret Begic was lying on the left side.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes. We all -- we heard you all from your answer. I'm sorry to interrupt you. I'm asking you about --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes, I understood. Now I will explain it to you. Now, he was on his -- kneeling above his head and holding his pistol by the barrel -- by the barrel. He was hitting him on the head. And he was striking him on the head, asking for the Motorola and what was our assignment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Will you please tell us in what hand.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Right one, the right hand. And Tuta had his right shoulder to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So if I understand, he had the barrel turned towards him; isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes. That's how he beat him. Yes. He was beating him with the -- with the handle of the pistol.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And only Tuta hit him with the pistol?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Yes. There. But before that, he was taken inside. When I was in the hut, they took me out and took him in, and they beat him there, and then they beat us over here, and then they took him out, and then they beat him separately.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Right. Now go to one page before. You have the statement in front of you. And look at the second passage. And that is what you say: "I saw a soldier beat Fikret Begic in the face with a pistol. That pistol had a Croat sign," and then in brackets, "the checkerboard." "He held a pistol in his right hand, and I think he held it by the barrel because I could see the mark on the handle. That is why I think that Fikret was beaten with the handle. That person gave the order to liquidate Fikret Begic." Now, that soldier, who was that soldier?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Tuta, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tuta. I see. Fikret Begic. And so that soldier, you say clearly "one soldier," and that one soldier was number one amongst them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Yes, that's him. Tuta, yes. I -- ordered to shoot him and the others off to Ljubuski.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Now, go down to passage 6 which begins as follows: "I had the possibility I could cast a glance at Tuta as I was kneeling." You see, "I was in front of the house where Tuta was beating." Now you say "Tuta." Now it's no longer a soldier.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Yes, Tuta. He, a soldier, naturally.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Mm-hm. "And I was 5 or 6 metres away, and I had my left side to the place where he was doing that."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So it is not -- it is not two different men, is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: No. It is not two different men. It is one. As I said, I was about 5, 6 metres away from him, and Tuta left, and he was beating Fikret there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I see. Thank you very much. I believe we've cleared this up now. And my last question, please be so kind - this is about Ljubuski - was: Were all of you treated correctly, generally speaking?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Not all of us, naturally.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did some people come? I mean they would come and beat you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Yes, one came. A huge behemoth of a man came.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did he beat you, that huge behemoth of a man?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You too?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: No. He asked me, "What's it that you have?" I had a many-coloured T-shirt and the others didn't. And then he hit, and then fainted, and then he went out and beat Dzemal Ovnovic and told Muharem Cilic -- he said to Muharem Cilic, well, had we been captured one hour later, he would have killed us all, because -- because Cikota was killed one hour after we had been captured and he had issued the order to execute every single man, every single male after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And who told you that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Muharem. And that's quite true, because when Denis came out in Sovici, after a while Salko Eglemovic was taken out and executed by a firing squad in Doljani. And on the 18th, we last saw him in Pasanica; Eglemovic, that is. We separated, and I did not hear about him after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I don't know. Are you answering my question or what? Because I asked you a very simple question, whether you were beaten by this big man who entered.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: No, he didn't beat us; I mean, not me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Well, that is my question. I didn't want to interrupt you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: No, but I wanted to explain who he did beat, and that was Dzemal Ovnovic, and what he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Mm-hm. Yeah. Well, and who told you that story that you were on the list and your commander -- I mean on the list to be shot when you answered?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Dzemal Ovnovic told us that Prlic had told him that the order had arrived from Tuta to execute nine men - that is, he and eight others; that is, we - because we were captured after three days because we had not surrendered. And he said that everything would be all right as long as we were in Ljubuski, but the moment that we left Ljubuski, he could not guarantee anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I see. Now, will you go one page forward in your statement. And look at what you said to the investigators. This same thing that you told us now. Look at what you told the investigators: "Later on, my commander from Sovici told me that about a month after we arrived in prison, the prison commander notified our commander that he and I were on the list of ten prisoners who were to be killed because we from the village of Sovici had not surrendered straight away. But the prison commander did not allow that to happen because the International Committee of the Red Cross had already visited the prison and registered us. He also told our commander that such things would not happen as long as he was in charge of that prison." And now, we shall move on for the Chamber's benefit. "After that, another 20 prisoners were taken from the prison," which is a completely different story, "and nobody ever found out what had happened to them. It was said that Tuta needed them for some kind of work." So you see, Tuta is not mentioned anywhere but absolutely nothing, any execution, that he ordered any execution - and this is what you say in 1997 - and you merely introduce Tuta here as if he needed some 20 prisoners. Outside the context, I read it on purpose for the Chamber so that the Chamber can get a full picture. Now, how do you explain that? You gave us a very nice story, how your commander learned it from the Ljubuski commander. But Tuta is nowhere to be found, nowhere.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: I didn't mention his name in the statement; is that what you're saying? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Well, that is what I said, but they simply didn't put it in the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Right. Tell me, please, now you are going to the Heliodrom; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So let's now go to Heliodrom; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Will you please be so kind as to tell me how were you treated at the Heliodrom, what was the food like, who guarded you, who commanded that camp, and so on.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: We were brought to the Heliodrom because allegedly at Ljubuski, we were called out for exchange, but we realised immediately that nothing would come out of it. We realised that they were lying. And there were buses parked, and we got into them and to Heliodrom. And when we went into the passage, and immediately we saw some who had -- I immediately saw some of our men who had allegedly been taken for exchange 15 days before that, but we saw them there. And after that, we started going to work, day or night, and we never knew when we could go to sleep and could have a rest. And it was Buhavac who beat us badly and Miro. That was a Bosnian. They were in the --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I could see that you are a narrative type of person and that you like to talk, but I'll ask you some questions. At the Heliodrom, there were only men. Is that correct, according to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: No, it's not true. There were also women on the third floor. There were some women there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: How many women were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Three or four.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Three or four?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: As far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Were they members of the army, too?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: I don't know. That's a different municipality. I never saw them. I could only see that there were some females there, and I think they came from Prozor because I didn't know them before.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And tell me, please, apart from those three or four, you were all men, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Yeah. In my department, there were all men.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And what was the food like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: We had one quarter for a meal; I mean, some pasta and things of that sort.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did you have three meals a day, breakfast, lunch, and supper?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Yes, but when the Muslims -- when the Muslim forces attacked, then at times they wouldn't give us any food for two days.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Could you take showers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Yes. There was one shower for 200 of us in three rooms or more.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Could you take as many showers as you liked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Why, yes, it was open. There was this passage, and it was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And did you get one quarter of a loaf of bread for every meal? For breakfast, lunch, supper, a quarter of one kilo loaf?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, who guarded you? Who commanded this camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: I forget the commander's name. There was Ante, but the name of Ante Buhovac, or Miro's, I'll never forget.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Right, fine. You've told us that already.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And did military police members guard and provide security for the camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Members of the military police, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I mean the HVO.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Well, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Were they at the entrance into every building and every room, and could anyone come out without their approval?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: No, nobody could get out without their knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think it is half past 5.00. And during the break, I will see whether I have any further questions, but I think I am drawing to the end of my cross-examination. I think I'll finish soon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll resume at 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, we left off at the Heliodrom; do you remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: I do remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And I believe that my last question to you was regarding the water Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. and the shower facilities. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And I think that the last answer to my question when I asked if you could shower as much as you wanted, you said yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And that you had plenty of water that you could use, as much water as you wanted to; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, we were also talking about the military police.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: My question was whether anyone could enter or leave without the permission of the military police.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: They could not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Were lists of men who were leaving made?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And when you would be coming back, these lists were checked; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Could anyone come and say, "Come with me," without it being registered and approved by the military police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm just controlling the record, Witness, for your information. Tell me, did you ever see the man whom you called Tuta at the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: No, never saw him there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I only have several other questions for you, which I consolidated during the break, and I'm just going to recapitulate things and take you back to Sovici.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You said today that the soldiers were wearing uniforms and some of them were black, and today you said that you had a -- that they had HVO insignia on them.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You also gave evidence today that the man whom you called Tuta also had a uniform.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you to go back to page 4 in your statement, page -- I mean paragraph 8 from the top, in the B/C/S version. And this is where you say this: "I do not remember what kind of uniforms the soldiers had, and I did not see any insignia." Page 6 in the English version. "I do not remember what kind of uniform that this Tuta had." I'm going to ask you this: Does this refresh your memory? Did someone else refresh your memory on this? How do you know today what kind of uniform it was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: I thought a bit harder, and I remembered that it was also a camouflage, multi-colour uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And the insignia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: They all had the same insignia and the camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, you said that you did not see any insignia. And that was my question.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: I did see them. I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So what is stated here in the statement is not true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: I did see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: As I said, what you stated in the statement, that you did not see any insignia, that is not true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, when you say about -- when you say "dress" or "clothing," you are referring to uniform? You're not referral to civilian clothes, like a suit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: No, no. The military clothing is what I'm referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, today you said to my learned friend about these two men - I'm not going to mention their names - that an order had come that they be executed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And that that Blaz did not allow that. Was perhaps he the commander? Was he a superior commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: He was not superior, but he knew Adis Tasic, and he moved him out of harm's way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Was he some kind of commander there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, please, where and when did you talk for the last time with Mr. Stringer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Mr. Stringer?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: The last time, last Friday.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And where?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: It is not important where. It was at this desk.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Well, I think it's just a matter of the location of the witness which, I think, is not something that is intended to be disclosed publicly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. You may skip this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I did not think -- I wasn't asking for an address. I did not ask for the house. I was referring to the country, and I think that that was clear. I'm not interested at all in the address, the house, or --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're not small --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The country is not important either.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, it's just that Mr. Krsnik did not really make, in my view, a sufficient enough question to enable the witness to answer the question without disclosing where he is now. He asked, "Where and when did you talk for the last time with Mr. Stringer?" So I'm not objecting to the line of questioning; it's just any questions which would tend to indicate the present location of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We don't believe that is essentially an important question, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we hear what country this is, perhaps that can be of importance, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I disagree, Your Honour, and I object to any questions which would tend to disclose the location of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: The witness has already answered, Mr. Krsnik. It's at that desk that's shown in the video, so we all know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These are questions for small children.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree, Witness, perhaps they are. Perhaps I don't understand things fully here. We would have to turn off the microphones. But you see that was the essence of our objection. The travel issue, if you can go to some other places, I guess I can say that I believe where he is, but that was my intention. But if he sat at this desk, then we all know where it is; right? Because if we rewind the transcript, we -- you can see that this took place in another country, and my colleague is going to try to find that place. Apparently that was in Bosnia. My colleague is just notifying me that this is what is in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I remember him saying that, but I think you're at cross-purposes. It was when he made his statement to the OTP that it was in Bosnia, but when he was talking to Mr. Stringer, it's where he is now. I think that's what he's saying.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Witness, this was my last Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. question to you, and I thank you for your cooperation. Thank you, Your Honours. I have concluded my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any re-examination, Mr. Stringer?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, just a couple of questions. You were asked about the location of the command post or the headquarters in Sovici, and you said that it was in the part of the village where -- you said that it was at Mr. Begic's house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what part of Sovici? I think you said previously it was in Begici. Can you tell us what part of Sovici Begici where Mr. Begic's house is located or was located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Across from the Kamen feature. You cross a river, and it's right there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Some of us have referred to different parts of Sovici as falling within Gornja Mahala, Srednja Mahala, Donja Mahala?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Donja Mahala. Gornja, upper.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you. You were asked about the conditions of your detention at the Ljubuski prison or at the Ljubuski location. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: I recall it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: During the day, did you and others go to perform labour at different locations outside of the Ljubuski camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: What were the conditions like?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is outside the scope of the cross-examination. I asked no questions about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Stringer, can you skip this question?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Could I respectfully respond to the objection, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may. You may.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Counsel asked about the conditions within the prison. Now, if the witness and others were taken outside frequently, I think the treatment that they received when they were outside the camp during the period of time that they were being held at Ljubuski falls within the scope of the conditions of their detention, and I simply wanted to ask about the conditions, what sorts of things happened to them during the day when they were removed from the camp and taken to perform labour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, with all due respect, after three months of evidence, I think that it is clear when -- regardless of whether we believe these witnesses or not, when they were let outside of the camp, they were under somebody else's jurisdiction. But I did not ask these questions. These are different circumstances, and other people were in charge of them, and we are entering into a completely different area that has nothing to do with the camp. They cannot be -- they cannot all fall under the same rubric. And this is why I did not ask any questions about what went on outside of the camp, because I did know where all he went, and then I would have had to establish under whose command, whose control he was, and I thought we had established all that after two or three months of proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Stringer, the purpose of the re-examination is to provide a chance to ask questions within the frame of the cross-examination put forward by Defence counsel. If you want to make a point, you have the opportunity to raise it in your direct examination. The re-examination does not mean that we'll give you another chance for your direct examination. So we advise you that you might skip this question, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President. I'll skip the question, and I have no further questions for the redirect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any questions from Judges?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I thought I had none, but arising out of a lot of the recent questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, you told us in your evidence that when you were in Ljubuski, you were registered with the Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: When you went to the Heliodrom, were you re-registered with the Red Cross, or were they aware of your transfer from Ljubuski to the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: They were not aware, but they visited us again and registered us again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Can you tell me, were all the prisoners in the room that you were in, the area that you were in, were they all registered with the Red Cross in the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Yes. In my room, everyone was registered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: In the other rooms -- if you don't know this, I don't want you to speculate. But in the other rooms, do you know that all of those people were also registered with the Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: I don't have accurate information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Thank you for being honest. That's very helpful to me. And thank you for answering the questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Judge Diarra.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Witness, I would like to ask you the following: When they arrested you along with your fellow soldiers, they took you to a man for whom you say that he was Tuta. They took you there, and there you saw that this was a man who was the commander of this group of men. Was anything said? In other words, did anybody address him? Could you conclude from their conversation that this man, indeed, was Tuta?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: When they took us prisoners, they said that they were taking us to Tuta. And I observed that this man was in charge. He was in front of the soldiers, so they couldn't have taken us to a common soldier. And I saw that he was -- the main one, and it had to have been the man in charge who said that those two were to be executed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At no point did anyone address him by the name of "Tuta." Would you be able to identify this man today? And if you are able to, could you look around the courtroom and see whether he is in this courtroom? And if he is in this courtroom, could you describe where he is seated and what he is wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With all due respect, and I would not like to be misunderstood by Her Honour Judge Diarra, I know that we have no right to intervene, but this gentleman gave a description now; and after all of that, I'm not sure that it would be quite fair that he be identified because the Prosecution didn't ask it, we didn't ask it. I just asked for a description. He said that he saw pictures in Sarajevo, so can I request of the -- of Her Honour whether we could avoid this because of the fairness of the trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, taking into account technical difficulties, we can give up an attempt on your part to make an identification in the courtroom today. But can you say that the man who was leading the men in the area where you were, can you say today that nobody had addressed him, but you concluded on the basis of the fact that he was in charge of these men that this was Tuta? Is that what you can confirm for us today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you for your cooperation and your honesty, and this is all I have to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any questions out of Judges' questions? And before that, Mr. Krsnik, I have to tell you that when a Judge is asking a question, there should be no interruptions. And in this courtroom, we don't put much weight on the dock identification, as you know. Yes. You may have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise, and I -- I know about this rule, and I apologise to Her Honour, and this is the first time. And I was -- I got on my feet with a lot of trepidation when I asked this, and I really did not mean to intervene in any other way. Of course, I have no questions. I would just like to confirm that, indeed, line 36 on 9.16.18.16, it -- I quote: "When did you last spoke to Mr. Stringer?" And he said: "Well, in Bosnia." This is in the transcript. So that's 36 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I don't think it's a significant point, but I think that if counsel insists to make some issue about this - which it is not clear to me what the issue is - but I think that we -- it may be preferable just to try to clear this up. I don't know if --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's not necessary, no. It is not necessary. My learned friend, I'm just justifying my question. It is in the transcript. This is why I asked where and when. And my apologies for interrupting you. It was just done not to waste time. I just wanted to avoid unnecessary discussion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, it will be fair to give an opportunity for Mr. Stringer to make any response on this issue, but we understand that this issue is not centrally important to the interests of your client. You may have the floor, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness just a couple of questions on this issue. You said that I met with you. Can you tell us, without telling us the location -- you said that I met with you at that desk where you're seated; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And that -- when did that meeting take place? Did you hear my question? I asked you when did I meet with you at that desk you're seated at.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: On Friday.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: That would be last Friday, about four days ago? Or prior to that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Prior to that, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Was it within the last couple of weeks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, did I ever meet with you on any other occasion, in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RR
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I guess there are no further questions out of Judges' questions. Witness, thank you very much for helping us by giving your evidence. We all wish you good luck in your future. The usher will show Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. you out of the room.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: At this stage, are there any documents to tender into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, we tender Exhibit 6.3, as it was marked by the witness, which is a photograph; that would be 6.3/2. And then also photograph 8.8, as it was marked by the witness, which is 8.8/1. And finally Exhibit, photograph 20.10, as marked, as 20.10/1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [In English] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. These documents are admitted into the evidence. Any documents from the Defence side to tender at this stage?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [In English] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So we will adjourn today, and we will resume at 9.30 tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 28th day of November, 2001, at 9.30 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 6.31 p.m.,
